statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. A real regional de-risking impulse has not become a one-way Nasdaq path. NQ trades near 29,133-29,142, up 27 to 36 points or roughly 0.1% on the 29,105.75 settle, inside a 29,017.00-29,155.50 overnight band that spans about 0.48%. Seoul opened 2.4% lower, extended to 6,408.82 for a decline near 4.3%, and has since recovered to 6,565.98, down 1.96%. The Nikkei 225 sits at 64,971.28, down 0.85%, off its 64,609.47 low. Monday's US session closed with the Nasdaq Composite at 25,980.19, down 0.76%, and the S&P 500 at 7,652.86, down 0.28%, on a semiconductor de-rating that took the Philadelphia index down 2.64% to a three-week low. VIX settled at 15.85, the 10-year yield is near 4.72% and the 2-year near 4.26%, and WTI has recovered to about 85.72 after Monday's Iran-sanctions decline. Tail is 10 in the low band because every market carrying the impulse has retraced part of it. Stress is 47 in the elevated band on the breadth of the Asian chip de-rating ahead of Wednesday's Core PCE, GDP and Nvidia stack.
recommendation: Descriptive only. The defining observation is a de-risking impulse that mean-reverted in every market that carried it. Seoul fell as much as 4.3% and has recovered more than half of it; Tokyo is off its low by roughly 360 points; NQ dipped to 29,017.00 and now trades above the prior settle. Mean reversion is functioning across the divergence rather than being denied, which is the direct opposite of the price path this measure targets. None of the required amplifiers is present: there is no reopen gap, no repeated extension after failed pullbacks, and the overnight range spans under half a percent. NQ holding the upper part of that band was reached by reverting off the low, not by extending from a trend. Tail therefore remains far below the block threshold, and the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON with a green status for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The flagged danger window spans 13:30Z-14:30Z, covering the US cash open and the 14:00Z Consumer Confidence, New Home Sales and Richmond Fed cluster. Every forecast hour maps to EA_ON because the conditional Tail path peaks at 18, below the watch band. Confidence is 86: the futures level, range and settle are confirmed by two independent quote sources, with live Nikkei and KOSPI levels and session ranges, yields, oil, the VIX settle and the seven-day calendar all verified, and one unreliable delayed volatility quote discarded in favour of the confirmed settle.
headline: Seoul falls as much as 4.3% and recovers more than half of it while NQ holds near 29,140 above the 29,105.75 settle; Tail steady at 10 with Stress at 47 as the Asian chip de-rating meets Wednesday's Core PCE and Nvidia stack
body:
The evidence that matters this hour is that a genuine shock retraced. Seoul opened 2.4% lower on the chip complex, extended to 6,408.82 for a decline of roughly 4.3% that breached the 6,500 level, and has since recovered to 6,565.98, down 1.96% and sitting near the top of its session range at 6,577.26. Tokyo followed the same shape: the Nikkei 225 traded down to 64,609.47 and now sits at 64,971.28, down 0.85%, having recovered roughly 360 points. Named Asian semiconductor losses at the open were substantial, with SK Hynix down 4.67%, Samsung Electronics down 3.34% and Kioxia down 2.49%. This is a real de-risking impulse, not a quiet session.

What it did not do is transmit into a one-way Nasdaq path. NQ dipped to 29,017.00 during the same window and now trades near 29,133 to 29,142 across two independent quote sources, up 27 to 36 points or about 0.1% against the 29,105.75 settle. The overnight band of 29,017.00 to 29,155.50 spans roughly 138 points, or 0.48%. NQ sits in the upper part of that band and has printed a marginally higher overnight high than an hour ago, and holding near a session extreme is one of the amplifiers this measure watches for. The qualifier is decisive: this extreme was reached by reverting off the low rather than by extending away from it, and the whole range is under half a percent wide. Every market in the chain retraced part of its move within the same session, which is the behaviour whose absence would define the pathological path.

Monday's US session supplies the backdrop. The Nasdaq Composite closed at 25,980.19, down 0.76%, and the S&P 500 at 7,652.86, down 0.28%, while the Dow rose 0.26% to 53,417.16 - a rotation rather than a broad decline. The Philadelphia semiconductor index fell 2.64% to a three-week low, with Micron down between 5.76% and 5.83% depending on the source, Nvidia between 2.03% and 2.91% and Broadcom between 1.74% and 2.63%. Delayed latest-session context confirms the shape: semiconductor coverage was uniformly negative across seven names with a mean decline near 3%, while megacap breadth was split five positive to three negative, with Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta and Alphabet all higher. That split is what separates a sector de-rating from an index-level collapse, and it is why the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.76% on a day the chip index lost 2.64%.

Cross-asset alignment is absent, which is the second reason Tail stays low. Yields rose only marginally, with the 10-year near 4.72% and the 2-year near 4.26%, each up around 2 basis points; delayed Treasury futures agree, showing the 10-year contract off 0.07% and the 30-year off 0.14%. WTI recovered to about 85.72, up 0.83%, paring Monday's decline that followed the new US sanctions programme on Iran, with Brent near 92.79. Gold firmed slightly. The VIX settled at 15.85, up 4.76% on Monday, and delayed volatility futures are marginally lower overnight; a delayed cash quote showing a 6% collapse was discarded as unreliable because the cash index does not calculate through Asian hours. Index futures are all fractionally positive and clustered within 0.08 percentage points of each other. Nothing here forms the aligned stack that would justify raising Tail.

Stress moves up two points to 47 rather than staying flat, because the breadth of the Asian de-rating is a real escalation in drawdown risk even where the price path stays orderly. A 4% intraday breach in Seoul on the eve of Nvidia results is a larger disturbance than the quiet drift of the preceding hours, and the catalyst stack immediately behind it is dense: Core PCE, the GDP second estimate and durable goods all print at 12:30Z on Wednesday, with Nvidia reporting after that day's cash close. Under the calibration applied here, a scheduled catalyst of that weight raises the probability of a large but recoverable drawdown without raising the probability that mean reversion fails, and the Aug 7 precedent - a large payroll shock that did not become a lethal no-retracement path - argues directly against pre-positioning Tail for an event that has not printed.

The forecast holds inside the low Tail band for all 24 hours. It opens at 10, eases to a floor as the Asian session ages, and lifts to 14 at 07:00Z for the European open, the same window that produced Monday's first structural peak at Tail 19 before fading it to 12 within two hours. The horizon peak of 18 falls at 14:00Z, where the first full US cash hour overlaps the Consumer Confidence, New Home Sales and Richmond Fed cluster; that hour carries the horizon's Stress peak of 56 and, with 13:00Z, the only event/whipsaw modes in the series. Conditional Tail then decays through the afternoon, falls to 11 across the CME maintenance halt, and settles at 12 as Asia opens on Core PCE and Nvidia day. No hour reaches the watch threshold of 20, because no amplifier has been observed rather than merely scheduled.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment. The window opened at 02:00Z on 24 August with Tail 9 and Stress 40 in a normal mode and held a 7-12 band through the Asian hours. The first structural peak came at 07:00Z, where the European open produced Tail 19 and Stress 58 in a trend-down mode; it faded to 17 within an hour and to 12 by 09:00Z. The window's only non-green slots surrounded the US cash open: Tail 20 with Stress 54 in an event/whipsaw mode at 13:00Z mapped to WATCH, and the single peak at 14:00Z reached Tail 26 with Stress 60 in a trend-down mode, mapping to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. That structure did not persist. From 15:00Z onward Tail collapsed to 13 and then held a 7-10 band for the remainder of the US session while Stress decayed from 54 to 42, the signature of a rotation whose directional efficiency faded rather than a path that denied mean reversion. The window closed with Tail 12 at 00:00Z and 9 at 01:00Z on 25 August in a mixed mode, as futures traded the low of a narrow overnight range and then recovered it - a recovery that has since held while Asian cash indices sold off and partly rebounded.
outlookSummary: The conditional path stays inside the low Tail band for all 24 hours, so every slot maps to EA_ON. It opens at 10 on the observed cross-market retracement, holds a 10-11 band through the Asian afternoon and the handover into Europe, then lifts to 14 at 07:00Z for the European cash open - the same window that produced Monday's first structural peak and then faded it. The series eases through the European morning to a floor of 11 by 10:00Z, lifts to 12 for the 12:00Z Barkin and ADP checkpoints, and reaches 16 at 13:00Z as the US pre-open, the Case-Shiller release and the 13:30Z cash open open the flagged danger window. The horizon peak of 18 falls at 14:00Z, where the first full US cash hour overlaps the Consumer Confidence, New Home Sales and Richmond Fed cluster; that hour also carries the horizon's Stress peak of 56 and, together with 13:00Z, the only event/whipsaw modes in the forecast. Conditional Tail then decays to 13 by 16:00Z, holds 12-13 through the two-year auction and the closing rotation, and eases to 11 across the CME maintenance halt and the reopen. It settles at 12 into the Asian opens on Core PCE and Nvidia day, where conditional Stress firms to 51 and Confidence tapers to 79 on evidence age. No hour reaches the watch threshold of 20, because none of the amplifiers that would justify it has been observed rather than merely scheduled.
